final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest AlphaMissense LOF-proxy signal (z=0.953) at the clinically relevant Ala222 locus; proline is absent from homologs and likely breaks local secondary structure to abolish catalytic activity.
Strong damaging proxy (z=0.842) replacing a bulky conserved Trp with a small thiol; Cys is not observed among homologs, consistent with folding/cofactor disruption and loss of function.
Damaging prediction (z=0.707) at the validated Ala222 position; slightly weaker than A222P because rare Cys occurs in a few homologs, so confidence is tempered.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ranking is supported by the strongest available phenotype proxy and additional evidence is unlikely to change the ordering.

history.rationale: Well-known thermolabile variant causing strong reduction of MTHFR activity via FAD dissociation and instability; strong LOF phenotype.
Retained as a well-known MTHFR loss-of-function/thermolability allele, but moved below A222P because this round's direct proxy evidence favored A222P more strongly.
AlphaMissense score (0.632) is lower than A222P/A222C at the same position despite A222V being the common clinical variant; kept in pool but ranked below the stronger Ala222 and Trp165 candidates.
The common A222V polymorphism reduces but does not abolish activity (thermolabile, retains substantial residual function), so it poorly matches a full loss-of-function objective.

rejection.reason: The common A222V polymorphism reduces but does not abolish activity (thermolabile, retains substantial residual function), so it poorly matches a full loss-of-function objective.

history.rationale: Conserved aromatic in the FAD/catalytic domain; alanine replacement likely disrupts cofactor binding and fold stability.
No new evidence was collected for W165A; it remains plausible as a radical Trp deletion but is weaker than W165C under the current proxy.
New score (0.665, pathogenic class) is higher than anticipated and above A222V, so W165A moves up to rank 4, just below A222C.
Alanine occurs at 17% frequency among homologs at position 165, indicating evolutionary tolerance inconsistent with reliably abolishing activity.

rejection.reason: Alanine occurs at 17% frequency among homologs at position 165, indicating evolutionary tolerance inconsistent with reliably abolishing activity.

history.rationale: A222P has the strongest AlphaMissense LOF-proxy signal in this batch and proline at Ala222 is likely to disrupt the catalytic/core region. It now leads the pool despite being a prediction rather than direct enzymology.
Strongest AlphaMissense LOF-proxy signal (0.953) in the pool; proline substitution at the clinically relevant Ala222 locus likely disrupts local structure and activity.

Highest AlphaMissense LOF-proxy (0.953) and proline never observed at position 222 among homologs, consistent with disruption; proline substitution plausibly breaks local secondary structure to abolish activity.

W165C shows a high damaging prediction and replaces a bulky conserved Trp with a small thiol, plausibly impairing folding or cofactor/substrate binding. Confidence is tempered because the signal is a LOF proxy, not measured MTHFR activity.
Second-strongest damaging prediction (0.842); loss of a bulky conserved Trp plausibly impairs folding or cofactor binding.
Strong damaging proxy (0.842) with Cys absent from all 23 homologs at this bulky Trp position; loss of the indole side chain likely impairs folding or catalytic-site geometry.
A222C is also predicted damaging at the clinically relevant Ala222 locus, but is weaker than A222P and less interpretable than the known A222V mechanism.
Damaging prediction (0.707) at the same hotspot as A222P; remains third, above the newly scored A222V and W165A.
Damaging proxy (0.707) at the clinically validated Ala222 locus, though rare Cys occurrence (4%) in homologs slightly weakens the LOF case versus A222P.
